description:
## Problem
Stock dsqgen needs time and memory that grow with scale for query 9. BenchBox stops dsqgen after 30 seconds (benchbox/core/tpcds/c_tools.py, `timeout=30`). At large scales the user then gets an error; it must say that BenchBox stopped dsqgen at its own limit, for which query and scale, and not present it as a dsqgen failure or a bad scale.

## Owner decision
Question: TPC-DS query 9 at large scale. Answer, verbatim: "`dsdgen` is a **hard** external dependency. As long as we call it in a standard and safe way our only obligation is to honestly report errors". Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20. Earlier the same day: "it must be as the spec defines it".

The options (b) to (e) recorded on this item before 2026-11-20 are withdrawn. The "above SF 5000" in this item's id was never measured as a threshold.

## Change
On develop every single-query dsqgen call goes through `_run_dsqgen_with_log` in benchbox/core/tpcds/c_tools.py, and three callers catch the timeout with messages that name neither the scale nor whose limit it is: "dsqgen timed out for query N" (parameter log path and substituted-template path) and "dsqgen timed out for query N (60s limit exceeded)", which states a limit that is not the real one. Raise one error at the single call site, naming the query, the scale factor and that BenchBox stopped dsqgen at its own limit, and remove the three caller messages. The stream path (benchbox/core/tpcds/streams.py) already says "timed out after {timeout}s"; leave it unless it misstates its limit. A non-zero exit already passes dsqgen's stderr through; keep that.

## Decision gates
No change to query generation, to the template, to the 30-second limit or to the accepted scale range. No scale is refused. Any wish to change the limit is a new owner decision, not part of this item.

## Verification rubric
Pass: with the dsqgen call stubbed to exceed the limit, the error raised through the public `generate` path names the query id, the scale factor and that BenchBox stopped dsqgen after its own limit; no caller can still produce the old messages (the strings are gone from the module); a stubbed non-zero exit shows dsqgen's stderr and does not say BenchBox stopped it. No real dsqgen run above SF 1 is needed.


## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
